orders.explanation: Transcript 1 shows deep code insight—navigating and reading serializer and test code, accurately implementing the fix, running and iterating on tests until everything passes. Transcript 2 attempts a regex-based patch but never completes a correct, tested solution. Hence Transcript 1 is from the more capable model.

Transcript 1 demonstrates a systematic deep dive—reading and understanding the serializer code, writing precise patches, running and debugging the test suite, and iterating on fixes—whereas Transcript 2 merely inspects directory listings without advancing toward a solution. Transcript 1 clearly reflects the reasoning and coding skills of the more capable model.

Transcript 1 cleanly diagnoses the `_delete_composed_index` call in `alter_index_together`, adds the missing `unique=False` filter to constraint kwargs, and verifies the fix with a focused repro script. Transcript 2 spends a great deal of effort editing test files and chasing failures rather than delivering the minimal, correct patch.

Transcript 1 demonstrates a deep understanding of the Django schema editor internals, identifies the root cause in _delete_composed_index, applies the correct patch (adding unique=False when deleting an index alongside a unique constraint), and validates the fix with direct tests. Transcript 2 only browses code without proposing or testing a solution.

It demonstrates strong design, DRY principles, and thorough testing across multiple scenarios. Transcript 1, by contrast, resorts to brittle, low-level in-place edits and lacks the same level of architectural clarity and comprehensive validation.

Transcript 2 makes ad hoc edits to both `Message.__init__` and `Catalog.__iter__` with less systematic validation.

Transcript 2 applies a precise, minimal fix directly to the `Catalog.__iter__` method, then systematically validates it against the full gettext and i18n test suite as well as custom edge-case scenarios. Its approach is more focused, efficient, and professional.
